newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria limps behind German shop hour plans.
newsitem.headline: Austria limps behind German shop hour plans.

text.p: Austria, under pressure from neighbour Germany's plans to liberalise retail hours, said on Tuesday it would change the law in January to give people more time to shop at weekends.
But the changes fall well short of those planned in Germany which is undertaking its most ambitions reform of laws adopted in the 1950s to protect corner stores from retail giants.
"The pressure is on because the new law should be in place by January 1, 1997," a spokeswoman for Economics Minister Johannes Farnleitner said.
The government published its proposals on Monday and invited comment from labour unions and employers.
Farnleitner's proposals would maintain the present 60-hour weekly limit on shop hours but would allow stores to stay open until 5 p.m. every Saturday.
Currently shops may open until 5 p.m. only on one Saturday each month. Shops do not open on Sunday.
Bakeries will be able to sell bread from 5.30 a.m. instead of 6 a.m.
Disgruntled shoppers often travel to Italy, Hungary and Slovakia to enjoy the more flexible opening hours, friendlier service and cheaper prices.

Austria's powerful unions and employers have so far stood in the way of more liberal shopping hours . Several months of talks have failed to yield agreement on overtime pay and more off-time demanded by unions.
